criteria.evidence: The measure names the test and the file (verify.rs) and says what the test shows. The diff touches only verify.rs (a new helper and a test), spec.toml and CHANGELOG.md. It changes no gate or verdict code, and Athena's replay shows 0 of 50 accepted readings newly refused.

findings.summary: Plain substring matching on common words can mark a case covered when it is not
findings.evidence: The keywords include "history", "cancel", "abort" and "nested", matched with `text.contains(w)` and no word boundaries. So a test about git history, a cancellation token or a nested struct counts as covering browser history, interrupted flows or nested navigation. A better approach would match whole words (or split identifiers on `_` and camelCase) and use more specific phrases.

findings.summary: Keyword lists miss common snake_case test-name forms
findings.evidence: The lists include "direct_link" and "go_back", but not "deep_link", "back_button" or "sub_route". Rust test names are snake_case, so `fn deep_link_opens_page` would be reported as missing direct links. Splitting identifiers into words before matching would remove the need for separate spelling variants.

findings.summary: status.rs was listed as an expected deliverable but is unchanged
findings.evidence: The diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, verify.rs and spec.toml. This matches the reading's fallback (the measure uses `status: not shown` plus a test name), so nothing is missing.

summary: The candidate adds `missing_neighbor_cases`, a small pure function in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs. It lowercases the added test text, matches it against keyword lists for four neighboring cases (nested navigation, browser history, direct links, interrupted flows) and returns the cases with no match. It adds one test and records the function as OLY-4-03's mechanism in docs/spec.toml, with owner Ares kept and a measure that names the test and ends in `status: not shown`. It also adds a CHANGELOG entry. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core neighbor` and the new test passes. I did not edit the function to test the revert, because my role forbids changes. Reading the code shows that a body returning an empty list fails the test's first assertion, which expects all four cases. fmt, clippy and the test suite passed in Athena's recorded CI run. The function is not wired into the gate and no verdict changes. The approach has two minor soundness weaknesses, both tolerable for a helper that blocks nothing. Plain substring matching on common words such as "history", "cancel" and "nested" can count a case as covered when it is not. The keyword lists also miss common snake_case test-name forms such as `deep_link`, `back_button` and `sub_route`.
